l4_steps.name: Extract GDS/NDC ticket sales data
l4_steps.input: Daily GDS ticket transaction files from Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; NDC booking records
l4_steps.output: Raw daily sales extract (tickets issued, voided, refunded) in BSP standard format
l4_steps.kpi: Sales extract completeness ≥99.9% of all ticketed transactions captured within 2hr of BSP cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC direct-connect bookings are not automatically included in legacy BSP extract jobs — manual intervention required to merge NDC settlement files, creating reconciliation gaps and delayed reporting

l4_steps.name: Validate ticket stock vs. IATA BSP allocation
l4_steps.input: Raw sales extract; IATA BSP ticket stock allocation records
l4_steps.output: Validated ticket list with orphan/duplicate flags
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket validation error rate <0.1% of transactions per BSP billing period
l4_steps.pain_point: Ticket number ranges allocated across multiple GDS channels can overlap when PSS configuration changes; BSPlink does not auto-detect cross-channel duplicates, requiring manual range-conflict queries

l4_steps.name: Decision: Completeness check — missing records?
l4_steps.input: Validated ticket list; expected transaction count from GDS settlement reports
l4_steps.output: Go/No-Go decision; missing-record exception report if No-Go
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness gate passed first attempt ≥95% of BSP periods
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS settlement files arrive up to 6 hours after cut-off due to Travelport file delivery SLA gaps, causing repeated re-ingestion cycles and risk of missing the BSP submission window

l4_steps.name: Aggregate sales by agent and BSP billing period
l4_steps.input: Validated ticket transaction file; IATA BSP agent master and billing period calendar
l4_steps.output: Per-agent sales summary with fare, tax, commission, and net remittance amounts
l4_steps.kpi: Aggregation processing completed ≤4hr after data validation; <50 manual corrections per billing period
l4_steps.pain_point: Sub-agents consolidated under a parent IATA code are not disaggregated in Amadeus Revenue Accounting, requiring custom SQL extracts to identify high-risk individual agents for ADM targeting

l4_steps.name: Calculate commissions, taxes, and surcharges
l4_steps.input: Per-agent sales summary; ATPCO fare and tax rule tables; commission schedule from SAP Ariba contracts
l4_steps.output: Itemised billing breakdown per ticket: base fare, YQ/YR surcharges, government taxes, agent commission
l4_steps.kpi: Tax calculation accuracy ≥99.95%; surcharge variance vs. ATPCO published rules <0.05%
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ/YR fuel surcharges filed in ATPCO are updated bi-weekly; Revenue Accounting must manually trigger ATPCO feed refresh — stale surcharge tables cause systematic billing errors affecting hundreds of transactions per period

l4_steps.name: Generate Agency Debit Memos (ADMs) for discrepancies
l4_steps.input: Itemised billing breakdown; expected fare/tax amounts from ATPCO; waiver/authorisation log from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Draft ADMs for agents with fare undercharges, invalid discounts, or missing taxes
l4_steps.kpi: ADM issuance rate within 30 days of ticket issue date; ADM dispute rate <15% of issued ADMs
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 850 ADM deadlines (within 9 months of ticket issue) are frequently missed due to backlog in Amadeus Revenue Accounting audit queues — expired ADMs result in unrecoverable revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Decision: Discrepancy amount exceeds $500 threshold?
l4_steps.input: Draft ADM list with per-agent discrepancy amounts
l4_steps.output: Approved ADMs forwarded to IATA submission; sub-threshold items flagged for batch review
l4_steps.kpi: Threshold review completed within 1 business day; 100% of ADMs >$500 reviewed by manager before submission
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated threshold alerting in BSPlink — manager must manually filter ADM queue; sub-$500 items often accumulate to material amounts across an agent portfolio and are not escalated

l4_steps.name: Submit BSP billing file to IATA via BSPlink
l4_steps.input: Finalised billing file; approved ADMs; BSP billing period calendar
l4_steps.output: BSP submission receipt and IATA confirmation number
l4_steps.kpi: Submission on-time rate ≥99% of billing periods; file rejection rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSPlink file format requirements (IATA Type A/Type B formats) change with each IATA resolution cycle; failure to update Revenue Accounting export templates before cut-off causes submission rejections with no same-day correction window

l4_steps.name: Receive and validate BSP settlement advice
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP settlement advice document; submitted billing file
l4_steps.output: Validated settlement advice with line-item variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement advice received within 3 business days of submission; variance analysis completed same day as receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA settlement advice arrives as a non-machine-readable PDF in some BSP country plans; manual re-keying into Amadeus Revenue Accounting introduces transcription errors and delays the bank reconciliation cycle

l4_steps.name: Decision: Settlement amount matches billing submission?
l4_steps.input: Settlement advice; original billing file totals; ADM/ACM adjustments
l4_steps.output: Confirmed match → proceed; variance → raise IATA billing query
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement match rate ≥98% first-pass; queries resolved within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP applies country-specific rounding rules for multi-currency settlements that differ from airline accounting system rounding — persistent $0.01–$0.05 per-ticket variances aggregate to thousands of dollars per period and are difficult to auto-clear

l4_steps.name: Confirm clearing bank receipt from IATA BSP
l4_steps.input: BSP settlement advice; bank statement from IATA-appointed clearing bank
l4_steps.output: Confirmed bank receipt entry in SAP cash management
l4_steps.kpi: Bank confirmation posted within 1 business day of settlement value date; 100% of expected receipts matched
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA uses country-specific clearing banks (e.g., Citi for US BSP, Barclays for UK BSP); different value date conventions and SWIFT message formats require manual mapping to SAP bank accounts, slowing auto-matching

l4_steps.name: Post BSP settlement to airline AR accounts
l4_steps.input: Confirmed bank receipt; per-agent billing summary; SAP AR account mapping
l4_steps.output: SAP AR postings clearing agent receivable balances; BSP period journal entry
l4_steps.kpi: AR posting completed within 2 business days of settlement; open AR items from BSP <3% of total AR at month-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Agent IATA codes in BSPlink are not always 1:1 mapped to SAP customer master records — new agents or consolidated GSA accounts require manual SAP FI configuration before postings can clear, causing AR aging issues

l4_steps.name: Decision: Settlement received within BSP calendar deadline?
l4_steps.input: Bank receipt date; BSP settlement calendar (IATA-published); SAP open item report
l4_steps.output: On-time: proceed to reconciliation; Late: escalate to IATA BSP country manager and initiate default agent process
l4_steps.kpi: Zero late settlements from airline side; agent default escalations initiated within 24hr of missed deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement calendars differ by country and are updated annually by IATA — treasury teams using stale calendar files have missed escalation windows, resulting in unsecured exposure to financially distressed agents

l4_steps.name: Review agent disputes on issued ADMs
l4_steps.input: Agent dispute notification via BSPlink; original ADM with supporting fare calculation
l4_steps.output: Dispute case record with initial validity assessment
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute acknowledgement within 5 business days per IATA Resolution 850; dispute queue cleared within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents submit bulk disputes at the 9-month IATA deadline, creating a volume spike that overwhelms the Revenue Accounting team — no automated triage in BSPlink means all disputes require manual review regardless of amount

l4_steps.name: Investigate disputed ADM with fare/booking evidence
l4_steps.input: Dispute case record; original booking and ticketing data from Amadeus Altéa PSS; ATPCO fare rules
l4_steps.output: Investigation outcome: uphold or reverse ADM with documented evidence
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation completed within 15 business days; <5% of ADMs reversed due to airline data errors
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical booking records in Amadeus Altéa PSS are purged after 13 months, making it impossible to reconstruct fare basis for ADMs near the 9-month dispute deadline — leading to unwinnable disputes and revenue write-offs

l4_steps.name: Decision: ADM dispute upheld by airline?
l4_steps.input: Investigation outcome with fare evidence; IATA dispute arbitration guidelines
l4_steps.output: Upheld: agent notified, ADM stands; Reversed: ACM issued to agent via BSPlink
l4_steps.kpi: Decision communicated within 30 days of dispute receipt; ACMs issued within 5 business days of reversal decision
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA dispute arbitration (if agent escalates to IATA) typically rules against the airline when documentation is incomplete — inadequate ADM issuance evidence (missing ATPCO fare snapshots at ticketing date) is the leading cause of lost arbitrations

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP settlements with revenue GL accounts
l4_steps.input: SAP AR postings; BSP settlement totals by period; revenue recognition entries from Amadeus Revenue Accounting
l4_steps.output: Reconciled trial balance; variance report flagging unmatched items
l4_steps.kpi: Month-end BSP reconciliation completed by day 5 close; unreconciled items <0.1% of gross BSP settlement value
l4_steps.pain_point: Timing differences between Amadeus Revenue Accounting (accrual at ticket lift) and SAP FI (cash at BSP settlement) create persistent reconciling items that are difficult to clear during month-end close under tight finance calendar deadlines

l4_steps.name: Generate IATA compliance and audit reports
l4_steps.input: Reconciled BSP data; IATA audit requirements (IATA Resolution 854); SAP FI closed-period data
l4_steps.output: IATA BSP compliance pack: settlement summary, ADM/ACM register, dispute log, defalcation report
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance pack delivered within 10 business days of period close; zero IATA audit findings classed as material
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 854 compliance reporting requires data from both BSPlink and Amadeus Revenue Accounting in a specific format — no native export combining both sources forces manual assembly in Excel, introducing version control and audit-trail risks

l4_steps.name: Close BSP period and archive transaction records
l4_steps.input: IATA compliance pack; cleared AR items in SAP; resolved dispute log
l4_steps.output: Locked BSP period in BSPlink; archived transaction files in AWS S3 data lake per IATA 7-year retention policy
l4_steps.kpi: Period closed within 15 business days of settlement date; 100% of records archived with retention metadata
l4_steps.pain_point: BSPlink does not provide a programmatic archive export API — records must be manually downloaded and uploaded to AWS S3, creating a labour-intensive process that is frequently deprioritised, resulting in gaps in the audit archive
